goal: Fix a wallet rescan bug where a transaction paying a look-ahead key is silently missed if a later transaction in the same block expands the key pool.
Affects rescanblockchain, importdescriptors, and wallet migration/restore paths, leaving balances wrong with no warning that a second rescan is needed.
reviewability: Needs rebase: labeled Needs rebase and the PR itself notes it must move into ChainScanner::ScanBlock once #34681 merges, which it now has.
An open design question (whether to switch to a retry-until-no-change algorithm) is still being evaluated by the author, so the current diff may not be final.
agreement: Concept ACK from achow101 and molnard, tested ACK (stale) from jeanpablojp, confirming the bug is real and the initial fix works.
molnard found an unresolved gap (spends of a recovered parent tx can still be missed); author declined to fix it here and documented it as a follow-up, an agree-to-disagree resolution.

jeanpablojp then found a further, broader gap (missed receives with no spend involved) and posted a working alternative algorithm; author is still analyzing it as of the last activity (molnard, jeanpablojp, achow101).

categories.name: wallet
why: P2 because it produces silently wrong balances during rescan across multiple wallet operations (rescanblockchain, importdescriptors, restorewallet, migration watchonly attach), which is a real user-visible reliability defect though narrow in trigger conditions.
Does not touch fund safety in the sense of losing keys, but a wrong balance with no warning is a meaningful correctness problem for affected users.

result.summary: This PR fixes a bug in CWallet::ScanForWalletTransactions where a transaction paying a key just outside the descriptor wallet's look-ahead pool is missed if a later transaction in the same block triggers a pool-expanding TopUp. The fix tracks the last vtx position where the pool expanded and re-scans the prefix before it, iterating until the prefix stabilizes. It ships with a new functional test covering loadwallet rescan, importdescriptors full rescan, and a two-level cascade scenario.
result.problem: Users of rescanblockchain, importdescriptors, restorewallet, and wallet migration can end up with wrong balances after a rescan, with no indication that a second rescan would fix it, because the wallet's look-ahead pool can expand mid-block in an order that hides an earlier payment.

open_concerns: molnard: a parent tx paying a look-ahead key followed by a spend of that output can leave the parent's output misclassified as unspent; author acknowledged as a real gap but scoped it out as a follow-up.

jeanpablojp (2026-08-29): found a further case where a plain receive (no spend involved) past the last recovered expansion is still missed, and proposed a retry-until-no-change algorithm that avoids the gap and benchmarks faster in some cases; author is still evaluating this as of the latest activity.
resolved_concerns: jeanpablojp's initial concern about the extra pass causing spurious -walletnotify re-fires and over-broad re-scanning was addressed by bounding the re-scan to the last expansion position rather than the whole block.
achow101's nit about using the for-loop bound instead of an explicit break was implemented.
molnard's suggestions to skip collect_range_ends() when SyncTransaction() returns false, use std::move, and consolidate the two loops into one were all implemented.
discussion.author_status: active, currently analyzing jeanpablojp's alternative algorithm before deciding next steps

The first (molnard, parent/child spend) was resolved by the author explicitly scoping it out as a documented follow-up, an agree-to-disagree. The second (jeanpablojp, plain missed receive past scan_end) is newer, broader, and still under active author review with no resolution yet, keeping the PR at Disputed rather than Positive w/ caveats.

categories.name: wallet
categories.evidence: Wallet label present; the change is entirely inside CWallet::ScanForWalletTransactions and directly affects rescanblockchain, importdescriptors, restorewallet, and migration correctness.
categories.rationale: P2 because it fixes a real, demonstrated defect where the wallet silently shows a wrong balance after a rescan with no indication a second rescan is needed, confirmed independently by jeanpablojp reproducing and testing it. It falls short of P1 because the trigger requires a specific mid-block key-derivation ordering that is uncommon, and discussion shows the current fix itself still has known gaps (molnard's parent/child spend case, jeanpablojp's plain-receive case), meaning the underlying problem is not yet fully understood or solved even by this PR's own contributors.

uncertainties: Whether the author will adopt jeanpablojp's alternative retry-until-no-change algorithm, which would materially change the diff under review.

Whether the newly found gaps (parent/child spend, plain missed receive) are considered blocking enough by maintainers to hold the PR, versus acceptable as documented follow-ups.
result.card: This PR fixes a real wallet bug where ScanForWalletTransactions can silently miss a transaction paying a look-ahead key if a later transaction in the same block expands the descriptor pool, leaving rescanblockchain, importdescriptors, restorewallet, and wallet-migration users with a wrong balance and no warning a second rescan is needed. jeanpablojp independently reproduced and confirmed the bug and the fix, and achow101 and molnard gave concept ACKs, but molnard and later jeanpablojp both found further missed-transaction cases the current prefix-rescan approach does not cover, with jeanpablojp proposing a more complete retry-until-no-change algorithm that the author is still evaluating as of the latest activity. The PR is labeled Needs rebase and its own description says it must be moved into ChainScanner::ScanBlock once #34681 lands, which has since merged, so the current diff likely needs rework before review is worthwhile. Priority within wallet is P2: a genuine, confirmed correctness bug affecting several important rescan paths, but triggered by a narrow ordering condition and not yet a settled fix even among its reviewers.
